2 | MATERIALS AND METHODS
In S06_Extended Methods, we present an unabridged version of this
Methods section.
2.1 | Mock soup preparation
2.1.1 | Input species
We used Malaise traps to collect arthropods in Gaoligong Mountain,
Yunnan province, China. From these, we selected 282 individuals
that represented different morphospecies, and from each individual,
we separately extracted DNA from the leg and the body. After clus-
tering, we ended up with two hundred and forty-­
eight 97%-­
similarity
DNA barcodes, which we used as the ‘input species’ for the mock
soups (S07_MTBFAS.fasta).
decision.reason: Berry2011positively reports empirical tag-dependent amplification/reproducibility effects, so it is not excluded as mere methods theory. Complete O'Donnell2016primary explicitly reviews Berry's one-step indexed-primer bias and two-step remedy, empirically re-tests the effect with replicate environmental samples/index tags, and reports the community reproducibility contrast. Current explicitly co-cites both for the same tested tag-bias hypothesis and tests same-versus-different tag reproducibility, without separately testing a Berry-specific T-RFLP finding or an additional intervention. Under the closest empirical-chain rule select O'Donnell2016once for this current comparison rather than also exporting the2011ancestor. This is not alternate-report/data equivalence, and distinct original samples or marker/method changes alone neither establish an extra pair nor exclude conceptual retesting. The raw independent2011positive opinion remains unchanged. Existing2328Elbrecht2017targets a different pipeline/error-reduction comparison and does not represent the tag-bias target.
